claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children under the age of 16, or do you have children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm inquiring about my child Alex. He's 21 though, so I'm not sure if that matters?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 21 years old, I need to explain that **Child Benefit typically ends when a child reaches age 20**, even if they're still in education or training.

However, let me ask a clarifying question to be thorough:

**Was Alex in approved education or training before they turned 20, and did you claim Child Benefit for them during that time?**

This will help me understand your full situation, though I should note that eligibility would have ended once they reached age 20.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I haven't been claiming Child Benefit for Alex. He doesn't live with me anymore, and I only help out with about twenty quid a week when I can.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Based on what you've told me, I can now assess your situation:

Since Alex is 21 years old, they fall outside the age range for Child Benefit eligibility. Child Benefit is only available for:
- Children under 16, or
- Young people aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training

Additionally, even if Alex were within the eligible age range, the £20 per week you contribute would likely not meet the threshold required to claim Child Benefit when a child doesn't live with you. To continue receiving Child Benefit for a child living elsewhere, you would need to contribute at least the full amount of the Child Benefit payment itself.

**Before I provide my final determination, I have one more question: Do you have any other children under 16, or any children aged 16-19 in approved education or training, that you'd like me to assess for eligibility?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex is my only child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to provide you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Outcome: You are not eligible for Child Benefit**

Unfortunately, you cannot claim Child Benefit for Alex as they are 21 years old. Child Benefit eligibility ends at age 20 for young people in approved education or training, and at age 16 for other circumstances.

If you have any other children under 16, or children aged 16-19 in approved education or training, you would be able to claim for them. Otherwise, Child Benefit is not available in your situation.

Is there anything else I can help clarify for you?
